native_payload.intent: Refactor-only PR resolving 13 SonarQube findings in soba, a Go CLI that backs up repositories from GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, BitBucket, Azure DevOps and Sourcehut on a schedule (interval or cron via gocron, or a single run). It decomposes runProviderBackups, displayStartupConfig, checkProvider, Run, checkProvidersDefined and TestGiteaOrgsRepositoryBackup into focused helpers; extracts the duplicated backup-status notification titles into constants behind a backupStatusTitle helper; deletes TestPublicGitLabRepositoryBackup2 as an exact duplicate; and merges Dockerfile RUN steps, sorts apk packages and quotes ${TAG}. The author promises behaviour and log output are unchanged, so any observable divergence from the pre-refactor code (log text or ordering, provider ordering, credential-check semantics, error paths, scheduler and signal wiring) is an intent mismatch.

residual_risks: Intent ledger (benign, non-observable): checkProvidersDefined (internal/backup.go:685-697) now evaluates bitbucketAPITokenComplete once before the map-ordered loop instead of inside it, so count is deterministic (1) where the pre-refactor code could count BitBucket once or twice depending on map iteration order when both auth methods were complete; the only consumer is the count == 0 check at internal/backup.go:712, so no behaviour differs, but it is a semantic tightening the PR body does not call out. (correctness, testing, reliability, adversarial)

Intent ledger (log noise under misconfiguration only): collectProviderBackupResults short-circuits bitbucketAPITokenDefined() || bitbucketOAuthDefined() at internal/backup.go:101, whereas the pre-refactor runProviderBackups read all five BitBucket variables unconditionally. GetEnvOrFile (internal/envfile.go:36-53) logs when a *_FILE path is missing, unreadable or oversized, so an operator with complete API-token auth plus dangling BITBUCKET_USER_FILE/KEY_FILE/SECRET_FILE now sees those lines once per run (from Bitbucket() at internal/bitbucket.go:19-21) instead of twice: a strict-reading exception to the 'log output unchanged' claim, arguably an improvement, and not a functional divergence. (correctness, adversarial)

Provider registration is now split across three structures: the new tokenProviders table in collectProviderBackupResults (internal/backup.go:105-114) carries the run function, while justTokenProviders and enabledProviderAuth still gate credentials; a future provider must be registered in all three or it will be validated but never run (or run but never validated). Not flagged as a finding because the shapes differ, but it is a trap the decomposition introduced. (maintainability)

Demoted #3 (P3, maintainability, anchor 100): internal/backup_test.go:629 and :632 call resetBackups() inside each switch case and the loop body calls it again unconditionally at :635, so every iteration cleans up twice. The same triple call existed before the refactor (c77f548 internal/backup_test.go:669, :703, :706) and the diff rewrote the block and kept it. Suggested fix: delete the two in-case calls, keeping only :635; optionally collapse the switch to an if/else. Report-only; roughly 2 removable lines in 1 file.

Demoted #4 (P3, maintainability, anchor 75, owner human): displayGitLabStartupConfig (internal/backup.go:271-273) passes "GitLab" to two log helpers and "Gitlab" to logProviderBackupLFS. This deliberately preserves the pre-refactor line `Gitlab backup LFS: ...` byte-for-byte, but nothing in the code says so, so the next maintainer will either 'fix' it (silently changing promised-unchanged log output) or stop to work out whether it matters. Options: normalise to "GitLab" and note the one-character log change, or keep "Gitlab" with a `(sic)` comment. Design call; report-only.

Scheduler and signal wiring (gocron singleton mode, waitForShutdown, Shutdown() waiting for the running job) was verified by reading internal/backup.go:30-38 and :503-556 against c77f548; gocron library semantics were not re-read from the module cache because the job definition, options and start/shutdown calls are byte-for-byte unchanged by this diff. (reliability)

callsite completeness: grep-only. Caller and usage checks for resolveWorkingDir, resetBackups, the title* constants, and the func(string) *ProviderBackupResults shape of Gitea/GitHub/Gitlab/AzureDevOps/Sourcehut in the tokenProviders table rest on text search plus a passing go build; no symbol-aware tooling was available to any reviewer. (correctness, testing, maintainability, adversarial)
testing_gaps: displayStartupConfig and the new logProviderOrgs/logProviderBackupsToKeep/logProviderCompareMethod/logProviderBackupLFS helpers: the PR promises log output is unchanged, but no test captures logger output, so a label or format slip in the templated helpers is invisible to CI. logger is a plain *log.Logger created in init() (internal/backup.go:660), so a golden-output test can logger.SetOutput(&buf), set a provider env (e.g. GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_ORGS, GITHUB_COMPARE=refs, GITHUB_BACKUP_LFS=true), call displayStartupConfig() and assert the exact lines and order. Reviewers verified the strings by manual trace only (all labels, including 'Gitlab backup LFS' and 'Organistations', match c77f548). (testing, correctness, maintainability, reliability)

Beyond the #2 umbrella: no unit test exercises checkProvidersDefined with both BitBucket auth methods (API token and OAuth) fully set, or with API-token auth complete and the OAuth *_FILE paths pointing at missing files; these are exactly the paths whose evaluation order and short-circuiting changed, and they are covered only by the credential-gated integration tests that skipped in this run. (correctness, adversarial)

Demoted #5 (P3, testing, anchor 75): backupStatusTitle (internal/notify.go:31-39) now decides the notification title for ntfy, Slack and Telegram in one place (internal/notify.go:94, :190, :222), and no test calls backupStatusTitle, notify, sendNtfy, sendSlackMessage or sendTelegramMessage. Suggested: TestBackupStatusTitle with cases {1,0 -> succeeded}, {1,1 -> completed with errors}, {0,1 -> failed}, {0,0 -> failed}, comparing against literal strings rather than the title* constants so a constant edit is also caught. The three constants were verified byte-identical to the old literals (hexdump) by reviewers. (testing, correctness, maintainability)

scheduleBackups/runScheduledJob interval and cron branches: no test sets GIT_BACKUP_CRON or drives Run() with a non-zero interval (TestGetBackupInterval only parses the value). runScheduledJob blocks on waitForShutdown, so covering it would need an injectable signal channel or scheduler; noted as unreachable with current seams rather than required for this PR. (testing, reliability)

The restructured Run() pipeline (validateStartupConfig, createWorkingDir, scheduleBackups, runScheduledJob), collectProviderBackupResults and the Gitea assertion helpers (assertGiteaOrgTwoOnlyBackedUp/assertGiteaAllOrgsBackedUp) are exercised only by credential-gated live-provider tests, all 15 of which skipped in this run; TestGithubRepositoryBackupWithMockAPI calls githosts directly and bypasses Run()/collectProviderBackupResults.
